title: Cross-domain functional-coordinate frontier map (selected completed screens)
hypothesis: Across selected completed domain screens, Mirror-labelled coordinates can be classified by within-domain quality/serialized-byte/compute frontiers, but a single pooled score is invalid unless metrics and controls are comparable.
physical_object: selected physical-sharing targets across neural operators, relational GNNs, diffusion controls and cellular rules
mirror_coordinate: domain-specific functional coordinate or code bank
logical_multiplicity: reported per experiment without cross-domain aggregation
controls: each source experiment's strongest declared domain-specific native control
each source experiment's independent-object control where measured

development.selection_metric: within-domain bytes_saved_percent and primary reported quality/compute; no cross-domain scalar

fresh.reason: meta-analysis uses already-committed reports only; no new audit data opened

selection.rule: recent completed scoped screens spanning neural operators, graph relations, diffusion control, NCA and online adaptation

storage.authority: source experiment actual serialized inference payload bytes
storage.paid_objects: Use complete payload byte values as reported; do not re-count or infer parameter counts

compute.normalization: retain each source's native MAC/operation/adaptation metric; cross-domain magnitudes are not pooled

success_gate: Produce a provenance-linked per-domain frontier table with no pooled score; identify where only generic compression improves and where Mirror-specific value is absent or not comparable.
failure_gate: Any untraceable bytes/quality values, aggregation across incompatible metrics, or omission of failed/null points invalidates the map.
boundaries: Selected recent synthetic/mechanism screens only; not the complete 1,155-candidate evidence base.
No experiment here establishes real-model capacity, quality or deployment gains.
A FAIL is specific to Mirror attribution in the source experiment; it does not negate a generic compression signal.
